owner: Public Code Security / PSR-15 recurring assurance
premise: For an honest browser/runtime executing the exact admitted FAE release artifact, the send intent presented to the user must remain bound to the canonical transaction payload actually authorized for signing; release/delivery provenance must make artifact substitution detectable.

current_fact.canonical_browser_source: The current repository main contains index.html, core.js, wallet-crypto.js, wallet.js and bip39-en.js.
current_fact.current_signing_path: wallet.js freezes a reviewed signing intent with FAEWalletSigningIntent, constructs the canonical transaction, rechecks current intent and transaction before and after asynchronous Ed25519 signing, and rejects payload drift before signature release.
current_fact.observed_assurance_gap: The prior direct-signing-path assumption is superseded by the reviewed-intent guard and substitution regressions already present in the Wallet candidate; exact-candidate integration verification remains required.

bounded_claims: This gate may prove exact-release binding and intent-to-signing-payload integrity under the admitted browser implementation.
This gate may prove fail-closed behavior for controlled payload/DOM/signing-call substitution mutations before signature release.
non_claims: No protection is claimed once arbitrary malicious same-origin JavaScript is already executing with wallet authority.
No protection is claimed against a fully compromised browser profile, device, OS, or user-approved malicious software.
A non-extractable wrapping key does not by itself provide same-origin script isolation.
required_evidence: Exact browser source is bound to an immutable candidate revision and release artifact.
The user-reviewed send intent is represented canonically before signing.
Browser regression proves destination, amount, network, inputs/outputs and any fee semantics shown for authorization equal the canonical payload passed to the signing function.
Controlled mutation of destination, amount, network, transaction body, or signing-call payload after review fails closed or forces a new review.
Delivery/release provenance proves the tested artifact is the artifact admitted for deployment; this does not grant deployment authority.
No seed phrase, passphrase, private key, or decrypted vault bytes enter evidence.
residual_after_contract: Exact-candidate cross-Lab, Wallet signing-integrity, browser and release-provenance verification remain required. The contract itself does not grant release or deployment authority.
